title: FaSTCC: Fast Sparse Tensor Contractions on CPUs
problem: Sparse tensor contractions are a core computational primitive in scientific computing and machine learning, but effective optimization through loop permutation/tiling remains an open challenge. Limited understanding of data access costs and memory requirements for different loop permutations hinders optimization.
motivation: Sparse tensor operations are increasingly common in quantum chemistry, scientific simulations, and ML workloads. Current approaches lack systematic analysis of loop permutation tradeoffs, leading to suboptimal implementations.
method: FaSTCC analyzes how much data each possible loop order must access from memory and how much storage it requires, using this knowledge to design a 2D tiling strategy (breaking the computation into rectangular blocks). To handle the unpredictable sparsity of real-world tensors, it uses statistical prediction to automatically decide whether each block's intermediate results should be stored densely (as a continuous array) or sparsely (only keeping non-zero values), and to choose block sizes that minimize memory traffic. These blocks execute in parallel using hash-based data structures to efficiently manage and access the sparse data.
key_novelty: FaSTCC uses a 2D contraction-index-outer tiling scheme combined with probabilistic modeling to automatically select whether each tile's results are stored densely or sparsely and to optimize tile sizes based on predicted memory access costs.
contributions: Comprehensive comparative analysis of loop permutation data costs
Tile-aware probabilistic modeling for accumulator/tile selection
Hashing-based parallel sparse tensor contraction implementation
Significant speedups on FROSTT and quantum chemistry benchmarks
